decision.observation: Steering was very costly again: 22 mph down to 6 mph from a 0.6 s W+A. The car is nonetheless centred on a wide gravel stretch, passing the boulder meadow with the fenced pool and lake on the upper-left; road ahead climbs straight and then bends right past birches.
decision.hypothesis: Steering at speed costs far more than the bend justifies (16 mph lost for 0.6 s). At low speed, plain throttle should rebuild speed along the clear straight.
decision.memory: New hard data point: W+A at 22 mph cost 16 mph — the worst steering penalty yet. Avoid any steering above ~15 mph; instead let wide gravel absorb gentle bends and correct only when the car is visibly off-road.
